name: When is an outdoor handrail required by building code in the Bay Area?

mainEntity.name: When is an outdoor handrail required by building code in the Bay Area?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Bay Area, outdoor handrails are generally required by the California Building Code (CBC) wherever there are four or more risers (steps) in a stairway or a ramp with a slope greater than 1:20. The CBC outlines specific requirements for handrail height, grip size, and load-bearing capacity to ensure safety and accessibility. It's crucial to consult with a local general contractor or the specific city's building department (e.g., Pacifica, Daly City) to understand the exact regulations that apply to your property and project, as local amendments can occur.
acceptedAnswer.description: Outdoor handrails are typically required by California Building Code for stairs with four or more risers or ramps steeper than 1:20. Local codes in areas like Pacifica or Daly City may have specific amendments.
